title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, retrospective and roadmap (Q2 2025)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates the current state and operating guidance for Platform Systems & Services (PSS) focused on dashboards, alerting, runbooks, the Q2 2025 retrospective, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended for oncall engineers, platform owners, SRE, and product partners. The guidance below reflects changes rolled out in May–June 2025 (see change log).

Goals:
- Reduce MTTD/MTTR for PSS incidents by 30% vs Q1 2025.
- Keep platform control-plane P99 latency < 200ms and request-router error-rate < 0.1%.
- Improve alert-to-incident precision (reduce false positives).

1) Services in scope:
- platform-control-plane: API + orchestration for deployments and rollouts (owner: Platform Core).
- request-router: global request routing and policy evaluation (owner: Edge & Routing).
- metrics-collector: Prometheus-based metrics ingestion and aggregation (owner: Observability).
- batcher: request batching service used by Hosted/Dedicated modes (owner: Serving Runtime).
- kv-cache: prefix and KV cache service used by runtime (owner: Serving Runtime).
- model-router: model variant routing and fallback (owner: Model Ops).

2) Dashboards (owner, intent, key panels):
- Platform Overview (owner: Observability)
  - Purpose: single pane of glass for platform health across regions and capacity tiers.
  - Key panels: 1) global error-rate (5m/1h), 2) request throughput (rps by service), 3) control-plane P50/P95/P99 latency, 4) capacity utilization (GPU pools), 5) active canaries/rollouts.
- Control-plane Latency & Errors (owner: Platform Core)
  - Panels: RPC latencies, DB replication lag, queue depth, recent deploys.
- Batcher & KV Cache (owner: Serving Runtime)
  - Panels: average batch size, batch wait time, cache hit/miss rates, per-model throughput.
- Observability Platform (owner: Observability)
  - Panels: Prometheus ingestion rate, Loki log throughput, Alertmanager queue, storage retention warnings.

All dashboards are in Grafana under folder: /platform/systems-and-services. Links: (internal) grafana.company:3000/d/PLATFORM_OVERVIEW

3) Alerting standards and thresholds (owner: Observability)
- Alert naming: <service>.<signal>.<severity> (e.g., request-router.error_rate.p1)
- Severity mapping: P0 (paging, immediate) | P1 (paging) | P2 (email + slack) | P3 (ticketing)
- Examples (apply to production only):
  - request-router.error_rate.p0: > 1.0% errors for 3m AND > 50 errors total => page P0 to SRE.
  - platform-control-plane.latency.p1: P99 > 200ms for 10m => page.
  - batcher.batch_size.low.p2: average batch size < 2 for 15m on >50% of GPUs => email to owners.
  - metrics-collector.ingest_backlog.p1: Prometheus write queue > 10k samples/s for 5m => page.

Alert tuning guidance:
- Set runbook link in the Alertmanager notification payload.
- Use suppression for maintenance windows and high-noise experiments; prefer silences over disabling alerts.
- Add runbook step to verify signal (is alerting on symptom vs upstream?) before escalation.

4) Runbooks (owner: Oncall & Platform Core)
Each runbook follows: purpose, pre-reqs, quick triage checklist, containment, remediation steps, postmortem trigger conditions. Below are condensed excerpts.

Runbook: request-router.high-error-rate
- Purpose: Investigate and remediate elevated 5xx rates from request-router.
- Quick triage (first 10min):
  1) Check Grafana panel: request-router error breakdown by endpoint and region.
  2) Confirm recent deploys (last 30m) on platform-control-plane / request-router.
  3) Check upstream services (model-router / batcher) if errors originate there.
- Containment: route traffic to fallback instances (use route: model-router->fallback) and enable degraded routing policy (akka: rollback to last-known-good).
- Remediation: if due to deploy, roll back via control-plane; if due to dependency, open escalation with Serving Runtime.
- Postmortem trigger: customer impact > 5min or > 10% error-rate sustained for 30m.

Runbook: metrics-collector.ingest_backlog
- Purpose: Restore Prometheus ingestion and reduce backlog.
- Steps:
  1) Check Prometheus write throughput and Alertmanager queue.
  2) If write_queue > 50k, scale metrics-collector group: kubectl scale deployment/metrics-collector --replicas=N.
  3) If disk pressure detected, follow infra runbook: increase retention temporarily and clean cold storage.

5) Incident retrospective (Q2 2025 highlights)
Summary:
- Two P0 incidents in May: 1) request-router outage (05-07-2025) caused by a malformed routing policy in a canary rollout; 2) metrics ingestion degradation (05-29-2025) due to Prometheus remote_write misconfiguration during a config roll.
Root causes & action items:
- Canary rollback automation insufficiently validated (owner: Platform Core). Action: add preflight lint + automated traffic shadowing for 1 week (owner: Platform Core, due 2025-06-30).
- Alert precision poor for metrics ingestion (owner: Observability). Action: adjust thresholds and add a heartbeat metric with synthetic writes to detect ingestion stalls earlier (due 2025-06-15).
- Knowledge gaps in runbook ownership for batcher (owner: Serving Runtime). Action: oncall rotation training and runbook rewrite (due 2025-06-20).

Retrospective metrics:
- MTTD improved from 7m (Q1) to 5.2m (Q2).
- MTTR for P0 incidents: 48m (May incidents) — target < 30m; continued work required.

6) Roadmap (next 90 days)
- June 2025:
  - Roll out canary preflight linter and automated shadow traffic for control-plane deploys (owner: Platform Core; milestone: 2025-06-30).
  - Implement synthetic ingestion heartbeat and refine ingest alerts (owner: Observability; milestone: 2025-06-15).
- July 2025:
  - Dashboard consolidation: merge redundant panels and publish team-level views (owner: Observability; milestone: 2025-07-15).
  - Batcher observability: add per-model latency percentiles and per-batch breakdowns (owner: Serving Runtime; milestone: 2025-07-31).
- August 2025:
  - Automate alert-to-incident classification using rules (owner: SRE tooling; milestone: 2025-08-15).
  - Runbook playbook refresh across all PSS services; publish clear owners and oncall training schedule (owner: Oncall; milestone: 2025-08-31).

Roadmap table:
| Quarter | Initiative | Owner | Target |
| Q2 2025 | Canary preflight + shadowing | Platform Core | 2025-06-30 |
| Q2 2025 | Synthetic ingest heartbeat | Observability | 2025-06-15 |
| Q3 2025 | Alert classification automation | SRE tooling | 2025-08-15 |
| Q3 2025 | Batcher per-model observability | Serving Runtime | 2025-07-31 |

7) Ownership matrix & contacts
| Component | Primary owner | Pager | Slack channel |
| platform-control-plane | Platform Core | @oncall-platform | #platform-core-oncall |
| request-router | Edge & Routing | @oncall-edge | #request-router |
| metrics-collector | Observability | @oncall-observability | #observability-platform |
| batcher | Serving Runtime | @oncall-serving | #serving-runtime |

8) Operational tooling & playbooks
- Use the following workflow for incidents:
  1) Acknowledge alert in Alertmanager -> create incident in Incident Management tool (PagerDuty/Incidents UI).
  2) Attach Grafana snapshot and recent deploys to the incident ticket.
  3) Follow the runbook and record timeline events.
- Playbook tips: always verify if an alert is symptomatic of an upstream system; look for correlated signals (logs, traces, metrics).

9) Oncall training and rotations
- New oncall engineers must complete: 1) runbook reading, 2) shadow shift with senior oncall (2 weeks), 3) tabletop exercise (quarterly).
- Next tabletop: 2025-07-10 (scenario: global batcher degradation). Sign up: #platform-oncall.

10) Change log
- 2025-05-08: Added request-router runbook expansion (Maya Chen).
- 2025-05-30: Synthetic ingest heartbeat implemented and alerts tuned (Priya Nair).
- 2025-06-12: Dashboard consolidation draft merged (Liam O'Connor).

Appendices:
A) Quick CLI snippets:
- Scale metrics-collector: kubectl -n platform scale deploy/metrics-collector --replicas=6
- Fetch recent deploys: curl -sS https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/deploys?since=30m | jq

B) Postmortem checklist (triggered when postmortem required):
1) Owner assigned and timeline drafted within 48 hours.
2) Impact quantified (customers, regions, duration).
3) Actions tracked with owners and due dates.
4) Retrospective shared in weekly reliability sync and confluence.

If you are an owner of a service listed above, please validate the runbook steps and confirm contact information by 2025-06-22. For questions, ping @maya.chen or #platform-core.
